model_name: Repressilator: symmetric cyclic negative-feedback transcriptional oscillator (Elowitz & Leibler 2000, Box 1, continuous deterministic approximation)
description: Synthetic gene network in E. coli built from three transcriptional repressors wired in a cyclic negative-feedback loop: LacI represses tetR, TetR represses cI, and CI represses lacI (i = lacI, tetR, cI; j = cI, lacI, tetR). Six coupled first-order ODEs describe the concentrations of the three repressor mRNAs (m_i) and the three repressor proteins (p_i). Each mRNA is transcribed at rate alpha/(1+p_j^n)+alpha0 (Hill-type repression by the repressor of the previous node, with leakiness alpha0), is degraded at rate m_i; each protein is translated proportionally to its mRNA and decays at rate beta*(p_i - m_i). The model shows that for sufficiently strong repression the unique steady state loses stability via a Hopf bifurcation and the network shows sustained limit-cycle oscillations.

variables.name: m1
variables.description: lacI mRNA concentration, rescaled by translation efficiency (average proteins produced per mRNA)
variables.unit: K_M per mRNA lifetime (dimensionless, see paper Box 1 rescaling)

variables.name: p1
variables.description: LacI repressor protein concentration, in units of K_M
variables.unit: K_M (number of repressors needed for half-maximal repression)

variables.name: m2
variables.description: tetR mRNA concentration, rescaled by translation efficiency

variables.name: p2
variables.description: TetR repressor protein concentration, in units of K_M

variables.name: m3
variables.description: cI mRNA concentration, rescaled by translation efficiency

variables.name: p3
variables.description: CI (lambda cI) repressor protein concentration, in units of K_M

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.unit: dimensionless (max protein copies per cell in units of K_M = (alpha+alpha0) in K_M units)
parameters.description: Promoter strength (maximal transcription) of the repressed promoter, in protein-equivalent units. Derived from the paper's stated values: fully induced rate 0.5 transcripts/s x 20 proteins/transcript = 10 proteins s^-1; divided by protein decay ln2/(10 min)=1.155e-3 s^-1 gives ~8660 proteins/cell; divided by K_M=40 monomers/cell gives ~216.5. The paper states the raw experimental numbers rather than this dimensionless value.

parameters.name: alpha0
parameters.description: Leakiness of the promoter (basal transcription). Derived from the paper's stated repressed rate 5e-4 transcripts/s (vs 0.5 fully induced), i.e. alpha0/alpha = 10^-3, consistent with the ratio alpha0/alpha = 10^-3 used for curve C of Fig. 1b.

parameters.name: beta
parameters.description: Ratio of the protein decay rate to the mRNA decay rate (paper's Box 1 definition). From protein half-life 10 min and mRNA half-life 2 min: beta = (ln2/10)/(ln2/2) = 0.2. NOTE: Fig. 1b axis is labelled 'protein lifetime/mRNA lifetime, beta', which is the reciprocal (10/2 = 5); the paper is ambiguous between beta = 0.2 and beta = 5. The Hopf condition is invariant under beta -> 1/beta, so both choices oscillate but with different periods; beta = 0.2 is the physically consistent rate-ratio value and is used here, beta = 5 is run as a variant.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Hill coefficient (cooperativity) of transcriptional repression; the paper states n = 2 for Fig. 1c.

origin.source_text: Elowitz MB & Leibler S, 'A synthetic oscillatory network of transcriptional regulators', Nature 403:335-338 (2000), Box 1 (deterministic continuous approximation); Fig. 1b,c
assumptions: Reproduce only what is written in the paper: the six coupled ODEs of Box 1, in the symmetric case where the three repressors differ only in DNA-binding specificity.
Time is rescaled in units of the mRNA lifetime; mRNA concentrations are rescaled by translation efficiency; protein concentrations are in units of K_M (Box 1).

alpha and alpha0 are not reported directly in dimensionless form; they were converted from the paper's stated promoter strengths (0.5 and 5e-4 transcripts/s), translation efficiency (20 proteins/transcript), protein half-life (10 min) and K_M (40 monomers/cell) by elementary arithmetic.

beta is defined in Box 1 as the protein-decay/mRNA-decay rate ratio (=0.2); Fig. 1b labels the same symbol as a lifetime ratio (=5). We take the rate-ratio reading for the primary run and repeat with beta=5 as a variant.

Initial conditions are NOT given in the paper. A small asymmetric perturbation was used for the numerical integration, because perfectly symmetric initial conditions excite only the (stable) s=1 mode and relax to the steady state even when the steady state is unstable; an asymmetric state is required to reveal the limit cycle.
No spatial dependence, no cell growth/division, no plasmid copy-number dynamics, no GFP maturation and no stochasticity are included (this is the deterministic continuous approximation of Box 1).

missing_information: Initial conditions m_i(0), p_i(0) are not specified anywhere in the paper (Box 1 only gives the equations and parameter values).
The paper is self-inconsistent about beta: Box 1 defines it as the protein/mRNA decay-rate ratio (=0.2) while the Fig. 1b axis label calls it a lifetime ratio (=5); the two are reciprocals.
alpha and alpha0 are only given implicitly, via raw experimental quantities (transcript/s, proteins/transcript, half-lives, K_M); no dimensionless value is tabulated.
The numerical value(s) of the steady-state protein level p* (solution of p = alpha/(1+p^n)+alpha0) and the exact Hopf/unstable-domain boundary expression are garbled in the available text of Box 1.

The stochastic model of Box 1 lists reaction rates (operator binding 1 nM^-1 s^-1; unbinding 224 s^-1 and 9 s^-1; transcription 5e-4 and 0.5 s^-1; translation 0.167 mRNA^-1 s^-1) but no initial molecule numbers and no simulation details.
